title: Man. Post. Cap. VII: GAR four dissimilarity heads; tip on separability
pass_a_gloss: GAR's second complaint: Placeus listed four dissimilarity heads—separable goods, other ways of losing, the judge's decree, sons being born and grandsons—yet when he explained the dissimilarities he said nothing of the first member. If a traitor's goods are separable by their nature, were not Adam's goods which he received for himself and his also separable—and in fact actually separated, lost by that first disobedience? So in this the dissimilarity is set up in vain. Tip into Placeus's reply on what 'separable' meant.
pass_b_english: GAR. Second, although in that explanation of dissimilarities there is what we may deservedly desire. For first, though four things were proposed—concerning separable goods, concerning other ways of losing, concerning the judge's decree, concerning sons being born and grandsons—yet when the heads of dissimilarity are explained, nothing is said of the first member. The goods, you say, of the traitor are separable by their nature. What then? And Adam's goods, which he had received for himself and his, were they not separable from him by their nature? Nay, they were not only separable, but were actually separated, seeing they were lost by that first disobedience. Therefore in this the dissimilarity is set up in vain.
source_text: GAR. Secundo, quanquam in explicatione illa dissimilitudinum est, quod merito desideremus. Primum enim cum quatuor proposita fuerint, de bonis separabilibus, de aliis modis amittendi, de judicis decreto, de filiis nascentibus & nepotibus: tamen ubi dissimilitudinis capita explicantur, de primo membro nihil dicitur. Bona, inquis, perduellis sunt separabilia natura sua. Quid igitur? Et bona Adami, quae pro se, & suis acceperat, non erant ab ipso separabilia natura sua? Imo non separabilia tantum fuerunt, sed & actu separata sunt, quippe amissa per primam illam inobedientiam. Ergo in hoc frustra dissimilitudo statuitur.

choices.choice: GAR: four heads; first (separable goods) unused—dissimilarity vain
